title: Choose the component language
question: The roll assigned Papeterie. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each picture is a working prototype of that direction (the board, the drawer, Réglages with the info card), drawn with Carnet's real font, colours, icons and emblems. Every option keeps your layout, behaviour, palette, Signika and the emblems; the left panel is full height and straight in all of them.

options.label: Papeterie
options.lineage: Japanese stationery: MD paper, Hobonichi, Traveler's notebooks
options.thesis: A precise notebook: every sheet die-cut with the same smooth corner, and on it your own things: index tabs, washi tape, the brand sticker.
options.viewport: Identical die-cut cards on the wall; pinned notes taped; each collection a divider with its name on an index tab; the drawer a full-height straight sheet; the info card a matcha memo.
options.risk: Two permanent ornaments (tape, tabs) where the research says one signature: either one spreading turns it kitsch.

raised.raise: Every card is the same plate: one die-cut, one paper, one edge; variety comes only from what is written and the wash chosen.
Chrome carries no ornament: search, bars and rows are type and line; the twists live on content alone.
Each card's furniture sits in fixed places: title, body, footer, tape always where the eye expects them.
Tape, tab and stamp are drawn inside the card's computed box: the wall never shifts for them.
Nothing is labelled twice: a collection's name lives on its tab alone.

options.label: Galet et feuille
options.lineage: Organic modernism (Perriand, Noguchi) and the Carnet mark: a sheet resting on a pebble
options.thesis: Text lives on calm sheets; state and identity live on the brand's pebble, the one organic form, which gives under the finger.
materials: smooth slabs, one corner for all
river pebbles in each collection's wash
options.viewport: Identical calm cards; every collection's emblem lies on a pebble of its wash; the chosen place, the open info and the capture button are pebbles.
options.risk: The most familiar of the four: its twist lives in motion and small stones, so a still screen can read plain.

options.label: Surface chaleureuse
options.thesis: White soft-cornered cards on a warm ground, big targets, one action colour that appears only where something can be done.
options.viewport: White cards on a warm ground, no grain, terracotta only on what acts: the capture button, the filled button, the chosen row.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and is the clearest of all; loses on identity: no twist, matcha and paper go, it reads like any friendly app.
options.risk: Carnet loses its family look with Bonsai and its paper.

options.label: Folio botanique
options.thesis: Every note a plate at the same scale and ground, hairline sepia rules.
options.risk: Engraved serifs and ornament fight the practical side.
options.case: Organic and calm, but decorative rather than practical, and its serif display breaks Carnet's single face.
options.kept: Every plate the same scale and ground.

options.label: Spécimen typographique
options.thesis: Type alone carries the page, no ornament.
options.viewport: A giant glyph over a grid.
options.risk: Leaves no room for the paper or the emblems.
options.case: A note board has nothing to specimen; it would erase the emblems and the paper.
options.kept: No ornament on chrome: type and line carry the hierarchy.

options.label: Jaquette de cassette
options.thesis: Ballpoint lists timed to fill the tape exactly.
options.case: Nostalgic and hand-made; loses both premium and clarity.
options.kept: Each card fills its measured capacity exactly.

options.label: Pochette Factory
options.thesis: Matte black, coded colour strips instead of names.
options.risk: Codes instead of names fight finding things fast.
options.case: Hiding names behind codes contradicts a board built to find things in seconds.

options.label: Catalogue de mascottes
options.thesis: Rounded mascots ranked in a pastel grid, each with its fixed name plate.
options.case: Fantasy without restraint: childish where you asked for premium.

canonCard.label: La norme du genre
canonCard.thesis: Google Keep on Material 3, executed impeccably: outlined 12dp cards, a full-round search bar, 8dp chips, a 16dp FAB.
canonCard.viewport: Keep's board in Carnet's colours: outlined cards, no lift, the standard drawer made full height and straight.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Keep by design: the reason Carnet exists goes quiet.

roll.assigned: Papeterie (Japanese stationery), candidate 4 of 7 on the grounded list
roll.pick: Galet et feuille (organic modernism fused with the Carnet mark), candidate 1 of 7
